stem:
Ruby is breathing fast but without distress and has a clear chest. Her heart rate is 190 bpm, her blood pressure is difficult to measure, and her capillary refill time is 4 seconds centrally. Her abdomen is soft and there are no obvious limb deformities.

Ruby looks pale and is showing clinical signs of shock. However, there is no clinical suggestion of bleeding from her chest, abdomen, pelvis, or long bones. Her haemoglobin is 65 g/L on the blood gas.

Which one of the following is the approximate circulating blood volume of an infant at this age?
explanation: The approximate circulating blood volume in an infant is about 70 mL/kg. This is the standard paediatric estimate used in trauma and resuscitation calculations.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury

rationale: The item is already a single-best-answer question and the existing options can be preserved. The standard approximate circulating blood volume for an infant is 70 mL/kg.

optionExplanations.A: Too low for an infant; this would underestimate circulating volume.
optionExplanations.B: Lower than the usual infant blood volume estimate.
optionExplanations.C: Still below the typical infant circulating blood volume.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: the approximate circulating blood volume of an infant is about 70 mL/kg.
optionExplanations.E: Higher than the usual infant blood volume estimate.
